# Management Services (SNMP, Syslog, NTP, DNS)

_Extreme Fabric Engine · 25 commands_

SNMP v2c/v3, syslog servers, NTP and DNS, including the exact `no` forms to remove each piece. Step by step removal and re-adding is in the change workflows (`ncs list flows`).

## Details

### `show snmp-server {community | user | group | view | notify-filter | context}`

```
show snmp-server community
show snmp-server user
show snmp-server group
show snmp-server view
show snmp-server host
show running-config | include snmp
```

`show snmp-server` alone lists the main settings. There is no `module snmp` for `show running-config`: the SNMP lines are in `show running-config module sys`, or filter with `| include snmp`.


### `snmp-server community <string> [group <group>] index <index> secname <secname>`

```
snmp-server community ExtremeRead group readgrp index first secname readview
snmp-server community ExtremeWrite group v1v2grp index second secname initialview
```

Out of the box the switch has `public` (read, secname readview) and `private` (write, secname initialview). The index is just a row name (first, second, third, ...). The examples are the Extreme KB 000078215 way to replace the defaults.


### `no snmp-server community <string>`

```
no snmp-server community public
no snmp-server community private
no snmp-server community-by-index third
```

Communities are stored outside the running config (Extreme KB 000115014): after a reboot they no longer appear in `show running-config`, and `show snmp-server community` shows the string masked. If you don't know the string, delete the row with `no snmp-server community-by-index <index>` (index from `show snmp-server community`). Extreme KB 000067212 says removing by index alone was not always enough on older releases, so check `show snmp-server community` afterwards.

> ▲ **Caution:** Add the new community and test it from the NMS before you delete the one the NMS uses today.


### `snmp-server user <user> [group <group>] {sha | md5} [aes | des]`

```
snmp-server user nms-v3 group nms-grp sha aes
snmp-server user nms-v3 sha aes read-view v3read notify-view v3read
```

Privacy (aes/des) needs authentication (sha/md5). Without `group`, give the views directly with `read-view`/`write-view`/`notify-view`. Because of the prompts, the command can't be pasted as a block with the passwords; automation has to answer the prompts.


### `no snmp-server user <user>`

```
show snmp-server user
no snmp-server user nms-v3
```

For users of a remote engine (informs) the 9.4 reference shows `no snmp-server user engine-id <engine-id>`. Check the exact form with `?` on the switch.


### `snmp-server group <group> "" {auth-priv | auth-no-priv | no-auth-no-priv} [read-view <view>] [write-view <view>] [notify-view <view>]`

```
snmp-server group nms-grp "" auth-priv read-view v3read notify-view v3read
no snmp-server group nms-grp ""
```

Remove with `no snmp-server group <group> [<context>]`, using the name and context from `show snmp-server group`. A safe order: delete the hosts and users that use the group, then the group, then views nobody uses.


### `snmp-server view <view> <oid>`

```
snmp-server view v3read 1.3.6.1
no snmp-server view v3read 1.3.6.1
```

Removal needs the view name and the subtree, exactly as in `show snmp-server view`. Remove every subtree to remove the view.


### `snmp-server host <ip> [port <port>] {v2c <secname> | v3 {authPriv | authNoPriv | noAuthNoPriv} <user>} [inform] [filter <profile>]`

```
snmp-server host 10.0.0.80 v2c readview
snmp-server host 10.0.0.81 v3 authPriv nms-v3
```

Check with `show snmp-server host`. Restrict which traps go out with `filter` and `snmp-server notify-filter`.


### `no snmp-server host <ip> [port <port>] {v2c | v3} <name>`

```
show snmp-server host
no snmp-server host 10.0.0.80 v2c readview
no snmp-server host 10.0.0.81 v3 nms-v3
no snmp-server host 10.0.0.82 port 1162 v2c readview
```

An entry is identified by IP + port + version + name, so copy them from `show snmp-server host`. v3 hosts are created with authPriv/authNoPriv but removed without it.


### `snmp-server notify-filter <profile> <oid>`

```
snmp-server notify-filter only-link +1.3.6.1.6.3.1.1.5
no snmp-server notify-filter only-link +1.3.6.1.6.3.1.1.5
```

Removal needs the profile and the OID, as in `show snmp-server notify-filter`. Delete or re-add the hosts that use the profile (`filter`) first.


### `snmp-server {name | contact | location} <text>`

```
snmp-server location "Building A, Room 1.12, Rack 3"
snmp-server contact "netops@example.com"
no snmp-server contact
```


### `snmp-server authentication-trap enable`

```
snmp-server authentication-trap enable
no snmp-server authentication-trap
```


### `boot config flags block-snmp`

```
boot config flags block-snmp
no boot config flags block-snmp
```

> ▲ **Caution:** Blocks your NMS too (XIQ-SE discovery and monitoring).


### `syslog enable`

```
syslog enable
no syslog enable
```


### `syslog host <1-10> address <ip>`

```
syslog host 1 address 10.0.0.60
syslog host 1 severity info warning error fatal
syslog host 1 enable
syslog enable
```

Default max is 5 hosts, raise it with `syslog max-hosts <1-10>`. Check with `show syslog host`.


### `no syslog host <1-10>`

```
show syslog host
no syslog host 2
```

`no syslog host <n> enable` only pauses that server. `no syslog enable` stops all syslog sending but keeps the hosts.


### `ntp`

```
ntp
no ntp
```


### `ntp authentication-key <1-65534> <secret> [type {md5 | sha1}]`

```
ntp authentication-key 1 <secret> type sha1
no ntp authentication-key 1
```

Remove the servers that use a key before the key itself. `show ntp key` lists the keys.


### `ntp server <ip | fqdn> [auth-enable authentication-key <key-id>] enable`

```
ntp server 10.0.0.10 enable
ntp authentication-key 1 <secret> type sha1
ntp server 10.0.0.11 auth-enable authentication-key 1 enable
ntp
```

Up to 20 servers. Check with `show ntp server` and `show ntp statistics`.


### `no ntp server <ip | fqdn>`

```
show ntp server
no ntp server 10.0.0.10
no ntp authentication-key 1
```

Remove the servers that use an authentication key before you delete the key with `no ntp authentication-key <key-id>` (`show ntp key` lists them). `no ntp` turns the whole client off.


### `ip name-server {primary | secondary | tertiary} <ip>`

```
ip name-server primary 10.0.0.53
ip name-server secondary 10.0.0.54
no ip name-server secondary
```

Servers learned by DHCP are removed with `no ip name-server primary-dynamic` (secondary-dynamic, tertiary-dynamic).


### `ip domain-name <name>`

```
ip domain-name example.local
no ip domain-name
```
